key_insight: Teaching a model to predict actions alongside video may weaken its ability to connect language with visual content. SWAM investigates how data and supervision can preserve that alignment during action learning; the provided abstract is incomplete, so specific methods and results cannot be confirmed.
problem_solved: World action models need to predict both video and actions from language, but action training can disrupt language–video alignment learned during video pretraining. Guidance on preventing this disruption remains limited.
method: Study language–video alignment when action learning is added to a world model.

impact: This work targets a key concern for practitioners building language-conditioned world action models: adding action capabilities without sacrificing language understanding. Practical recommendations and performance gains cannot be assessed from the excerpt.
